brief: Hashes, signs and ciphers a text: SHA-256, MD5, BLAKE3, HMAC, base64, and the classic toy ciphers.
detail: It is the crypto helper of stzString. Build it with StzStringCryptoQ over a text, or with new stzStringCrypto, and keep the text and the key apart: the digests are engine-backed and match the published test vectors (abc gives ba7816bf... under SHA-256). The ciphers (ROT13, Caesar, Vigenere, Atbash, ROT47, XOR, Obfuscate) are toys that hide text from a glance and are not encryption: they only move the Latin letters or the ASCII range, so Hebrew, Arabic and emoji pass through unchanged, while the digests, base64 and XOR work on UTF-8 bytes. A verb without an ending (ROT13, Atbash) changes the held text and returns nothing, the form ending in -ed (ROT13ed, Atbashed, CaesarEncrypted) returns the new text and leaves the helper alone. Pass a plain text, not a stzString object: editing through the helper empties the stzString that was passed in. IsEncrypted answers TRUE for almost any text today.
